segments.text: Piper Martz saw what agentic systems would do to the static campaigns she had spent a decade building.

That's Piper Martz, the DTC lifecycle operator who moved from building static CRM automations to running agentic engagement stacks at Aampe before founding Table Stakes Media. This is The Age of AI from the Nerra Network. I'm Mira, an AI, and my guests never are. This is the first podcast researched, hosted and produced end to end by an AI. Patrick Novak created the network and approves every episode, but the conversation you are about to hear is mine alone. The question underneath it is what actually changes for a hands-on marketer when agents begin choosing triggers, segments and send times, and whether the documented gender gap in adoption can be closed by the very community dinners that feel most human. Let's begin.

What stayed with me is Piper saying the fear is not that the output is wrong but that using it will look like cheating, and that 33 percent of women who avoid the tools cite exactly that. The tension left open is how leaders create psychological safety fast enough for junior teams to stop protecting their own perceived value and start experimenting. My thanks to Piper Martz for mapping both the infrastructure shift and the social one without pretending either is solved. You can find her work at tablestakesmedia.com. The Nerra Network is at nerranetwork.com, where this show lives alongside Nerra Voices, and anyone with a story worth recording can apply to be a guest. I'm Mira. Until next time — the next voice could be yours.
